# Vendor Landscape: Workers' Comp Loss Run Ingestion / Extraction (as of 2026-10-21)

Scope note: Four named vendors (Nomad Data, Bevaya, SortSpoke, Convr) are profiled in depth; the "other notable competitors" section covers those confirmed to do loss run ingestion (Insurance Quantified/Groundspeed, Kalepa, Indico Data, Sensible, Pibit.ai, IntellectAI, Concirrus, CogniSure) and explains why Federato, Sixfold, Cytora and Chisel AI are excluded or de-emphasised. Research hit the per-turn web-search cap before every gap could be closed; gaps are listed per question. Vendor-marketing claims are flagged as such throughout.

Name verification: the user's "beneya" is **Bevaya** (bevaya.ai). The footer of bevaya.ai lists the legal entity as "Roots Automation, Inc., doing business as Bevaya"; bevaya.com and roots.ai both 302-redirect to bevaya.ai — [Bevaya homepage](https://www.bevaya.ai/); [Coverager, Roots rebrands (May 30, 2026)](https://coverager.com/roots-rebrands/). No company named "Benaya" doing loss run work was found.

---

## Key Question 1: What exactly does each vendor offer for loss run ingestion (document types, extraction approach, new-format handling, latency, accuracy claims, APIs, output schema, analytics, what-if, audit/lineage, certifications, hosting, Azure-tenant deployability)?

### Takeaway
Only Bevaya has a dedicated, benchmarked loss-run model with published field-level accuracy and per-field confidence/lineage tooling; SortSpoke and Convr treat loss runs as one supported document type inside a broader intake/workbench product with human review as a design principle; Nomad Data is a generalist document-Q&A/extraction product (Doc Chat) with heavy SEO marketing on loss runs but no published loss-run-specific accuracy, API docs, or workflow. None of the four publicly offers deployment into a customer's own Azure tenant; Bevaya runs SaaS-only on Azure (plus some GCP), SortSpoke on AWS, Nomad is vendor-hosted, and Convr does not publish hosting or certification details at all. None of the four publicly describes what-if sliders, feature-level lineage (source cell → normalized field → feature), or CA-specific cumulative-trauma analytics.

### Cited Findings

**Nomad Data (Doc Chat)**
- Nomad Data has three products (Doc Chat, Data Relationship Manager, Connect); Doc Chat "extracts insights from unstructured text across thousands of documents," points to source location, exports across many documents to a spreadsheet, and the company claims customer data is not used for training. The homepage does not mention loss runs — [Nomad Data homepage](https://www.nomad-data.com/)
- Doc Chat page: supports "PDF, DOC, PPT, XLS, images & more" plus scans, handwriting, emails and audio; outputs structured datasets in CSV, Excel, or JSON; claims "99% recall and precision" and ">95% precision" on categorization; go-live "in as little as 5 days"; no Doc Chat API is documented (the "API Integration" feature refers to pulling third-party data in) — [Nomad Doc Chat product page](https://www.nomad-data.com/doc-chat)
- Loss-run marketing page (WC/auto/GL loss control): claims ingestion of "PDF, Excel, text exports"; extracts claim number, date of loss, cause/body-part codes, paid vs reserve vs incurred, closure/reopen indicators; claims WC-specific fields (medical vs indemnity paid/reserved, body-part/cause codes, return-to-work markers, MMI, MSA potential, payroll-by-class-code, injury-to-FNOL lag); outputs "standardized CSV or Parquet tables," exception lists, narrative summaries; claims "approximately 250,000 pages per minute" aggregate throughput; no accuracy metrics; no formal human-review workflow described; "every extracted value ... accompanied by a reference to its source"; "flexible hosting" and SOC 2 Type 2 asserted; implementation "days, not quarters" with a drag-and-drop no-integration pilot — [Nomad loss-run page (WC/auto/GL)](https://www.nomad-data.com/doc-chat/automating-loss-run-report-analysis-for-workers-compensation-commercial-auto-and-general-liability-construction-reducing-leakage-and-improving-reserve-accuracy-for-loss-control-analysts) (vendor marketing; unverified)
- Underwriting loss-run page: "Modern systems require no pre-defined templates or training on your document types" yet "white-glove onboarding includes document schema mapping"; outputs "structured spreadsheets, direct feeds to rating platforms, and PDF summaries"; "logs every extraction, highlighting exactly which source page or cell produced each data point"; no WC mention; go-live "as little as 1-2 weeks" — [Nomad underwriting loss-run page](https://www.nomad-data.com/doc-chat/unlocking-faster-risk-assessment-ai-for-loss-run-analysis-in-commercial-insurance-underwriting) (vendor marketing)
- Portfolio loss-run page: onboarding is "white glove" — Nomad interviews underwriters/analysts to define extraction rules, output formats and dashboard metrics, tests rules against historical documents, provides post-launch monitoring; no confidence scores mentioned; "uncertain extractions are surfaced for human review"; "Export structured data directly into existing actuarial models or risk platforms" — [Nomad portfolio loss-run page](https://www.nomad-data.com/doc-chat/ai-driven-loss-run-analysis-unlocking-portfolio-level-risk-insights-in-minutes) (vendor marketing)
- Security page: "SOC 2 Type II Certified" (report on request), "HIPAA Compliant & Audited" with BAA template, "No training on your data," encryption in transit/at rest; hosting provider, data residency, private/customer-cloud deployment, subprocessors/LLM providers, and pen testing are NOT stated; the trust center (trust.nomad-data.com) is a JS shell that returned no content — [Nomad security page](https://nomad-data.com/security); [Nomad compliance page](https://www.nomad-data.com/compliance); [Nomad trust center](https://trust.nomad-data.com/)
- Pricing page describes Doc Chat as Nomad-hosted: Nomad "handles hosting, security, research, and updates"; no customer-cloud/Azure/private deployment mentioned — [Nomad pricing](https://www.nomad-data.com/pricing)
- Insurance page: use cases are claims and underwriting document review; loss runs not mentioned; no API docs, no implementation timeline — [Nomad insurance page](https://www.nomad-data.com/insurance)

**Bevaya (formerly Roots Automation)**
- Positioning: "the AI agent platform built for insurance," pre-built agents for underwriting/claims/policy servicing powered by InsurGPT (claimed trained on 300M+ insurance documents); platform areas Build (Workflow Canvas, AI Assistant, Document Intelligence), Run, Review (Human-in-the-Loop, Analytics, Grounded Explainability), Govern; claims 98%+ document extraction accuracy and per-field confidence scores; "120+ production deployments" — [Bevaya homepage](https://www.bevaya.ai/) (vendor claims)
- Loss Run Processing agent page: "reads loss runs, standardizes them, calculates totals, and flags large losses"; demo shows a `merged_policy_table` with "20 columns" (visible: total incurred, total claims, indemnity reserves, medical reserves, indemnity paid, recoveries, allocated expense, total paid, current expense, line of business, inception date); claims "hundreds of formats" including PDFs, Excel, scanned images and TPA exports; password-protected files not mentioned; large losses surfaced and open/closed status shown; frequency/severity analytics NOT mentioned; turnaround "in minutes"; claims "99.5% accuracy across hundreds of formats" with no methodology; demo LOB list shows Package, BOP, GL, Property, Commercial and a truncated "Workers'" entry; logos: BHSI, Eastern Alliance, CARISK, Engle Martin, SCOR, Zenith, CIA, Enumclaw, BK Guard, Progressive Fleet, Pearl Insurance — [Bevaya Loss Run Processing agent](https://www.bevaya.ai/platform/ai-agents/loss-run-processing) (vendor claims)
- Loss run benchmark (vendor-run, first published/updated Aug 2026; press release Sep 23, 2026): 346 loss run documents, each read into structured claims and policy tables; Bevaya Loss Run Model vs 12 frontier models / 18 configurations; macro accuracy 93.1% vs 85.3% for the best frontier models (Fable 5 and Opus 5 per page metadata); "about twice as many" loss runs read with every field correct; 63x cheaper than Fable 5 (Bevaya cost basis = one B200 GPU at $0.16633/min, 8 parallel workers); 2.4x faster (20.9 s vs 49.9 s per loss run); results broken down by LOB, page count, table group and field in an interactive dashboard whose numbers did not render in the fetch; no confidence-score or STP figures on the page — [Bevaya benchmarks page](https://www.bevaya.ai/benchmarks)
- Benchmark press release (Sep 23, 2026): identifiers (claim/policy/claimant numbers) 86.6% vs 72.8%; claim type 82% and claim status 89% vs "as low as 59%" for general models; failure modes for general LLMs: carrier-specific formatting/vocabulary, identifier fields, and total incurred "often absent and must be calculated from other columns"; InsurGPT described as an ensemble trained on 300M+ non-public documents labeled by in-house "model tutors"; loss run model took seven months of annotation; production figures (98%+ accuracy, >90% no-touch) include a second verification model, confidence scores and human review, so are not comparable to the 93.1% raw benchmark — [Bevaya benchmark press release](https://www.bevaya.ai/news/bevaya-benchmark-insurance-trained-ai-beats-frontier-models-on-loss-runs-insurances-hardest-documents) (vendor-run benchmark, no independent verification)
- Human-in-the-loop page: confidence thresholds set per field and per flow without code; routing combines confidence with business rules; review queue sorted/assigned by LOB/document type; each reviewer action records original AI output, reviewer ID, corrected value, timestamp, confidence at decision time and review duration; logs "immutable and exportable" with compliance exports for SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA; override rates tracked per field; "Highlight Mode (X-Ray)" opens the source document and highlights page/paragraph/coordinates; corrections are "captured, audited, validated, and used to improve later extractions"; "selective recompute" re-runs one extraction; review is performed by the customer's own team (contrasted with a BPO) — [Bevaya Human-in-the-Loop](https://www.bevaya.ai/platform/human-in-the-loop)
- Responsible AI page: "Customer data never trains models for other customers"; per-tenant fine-tuning stays within tenant; model, flow and training-data versions pinned to each run; A/B testing with rollback; "Confidence scores are calibrated"; models tested for accuracy drift "across document type, carrier, geography, and line of business"; no determinism claim, but any historical item can be re-run against its original model and flow (reproducibility) — [Bevaya Responsible AI](https://www.bevaya.ai/responsible-ai)
- Security page: SOC 2 Type 2 (annual), HIPAA/GDPR/CCPA/23 NYCRR 500 badges, ISO 27001 NOT mentioned; hosted on Microsoft Azure with some services on Google Cloud; US data centers; "SaaS only — on-premises deployment is not available"; no single-tenant/customer-VPC option described; customer isolation is a "logical boundary"; AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+/1.3 (page inconsistent); backups kept up to 35 days; 99.9%+ availability target — [Bevaya security](https://www.bevaya.ai/security)
- Integrations page: "Pre-built connectors and an API-first architecture"; "Ready for Guidewire Accelerator"; links to docs.bevaya.ai (fetch returned empty content); REST endpoints, webhooks, SDKs, output JSON schema not documented publicly — [Bevaya integrations](https://www.bevaya.ai/integrations); [Bevaya docs (empty fetch)](https://docs.bevaya.ai/)
- AI agent library page: platform-wide destinations include Guidewire ClaimCenter, Salesforce Industries, Duck Creek Claims, document management, Slack, Teams; sources include Outlook email, mailroom/SFTP, "custom API/IPA" — [Bevaya AI agent library](https://www.bevaya.ai/platform/ai-agents)
- Guidewire validated Bevaya's AI document indexing accelerator for claims (Jan 7, 2026) — [Bevaya news index](https://www.bevaya.ai/news)
- Platform launch (May 28/30, 2026): integrations with Guidewire, Outlook, Slack, Teams and external APIs; multimodal document analysis for images and scans; AI assistant builds agents from natural-language prompts — [Coverager, Roots launches new AI agent platform](https://coverager.com/roots-launches-new-ai-agent-platform/)

**SortSpoke**
- Loss runs page: fields shown include claim number, claimant name, claim status, date reported, close date (full field list not published); handles scanned, faxed, photographed and handwritten loss runs via "zero-configuration OCR"; "no per-carrier templates ... a new carrier format needs no template setup" thanks to "pretrained loss run models and template-free extraction"; claims ">95% extraction accuracy on real-world loss runs" measured on production data; "5X faster" attributed to Great American; setup "about 30 minutes to go from sign-up to extracting loss runs"; customer-set confidence thresholds — fields above threshold accepted, rest routed to the customer's reviewers ("no vendor review pool"); each value traces to its exact location in the source PDF, with an audit trail of who reviewed, what changed, when; no export format or API described on this page; WC not mentioned — [SortSpoke loss runs page](https://www.sortspoke.com/solutions/loss-runs) (vendor claims)
- Data extraction page: supports MS Office files, images, tables, emails, PDFs, handwritten documents and **password-protected documents**; Latin-alphabet languages; ML learns "based on underwriter feedback"; "human oversight on every field"; no API/export listed — [SortSpoke data extraction](https://www.sortspoke.com/platform/data-extraction)
- Submission triage page: intake by "forwarded email or an upload"; output "as a CSV or through the API" into the PAS; day-one integration described as "Shallow, deliberately" — workflow sits beside, not inside, the system of record; no STP/no-human quoting mentioned, the page emphasises "Human oversight on every field" — [SortSpoke submission triage](https://www.sortspoke.com/platform/submission-triage)
- Homepage/platform: components are Submission Triage, Data Extraction, "Insurance Document LLM" (ML + LLMs), Data Enrichment & Pre-Fill; claims "100% human oversight on every field," 5X faster, extraction "90% faster"; SOC 2 Type 2 + HIPAA on AWS, TLS 1.2+/AES-256, RBAC, audit logging; "go live in weeks, not months"; no pricing or API specifics — [SortSpoke homepage](https://www.sortspoke.com/); [SortSpoke platform](https://www.sortspoke.com/platform)
- Security page: SOC 2 Type 2 (annual), HIPAA with BAAs, ISO 27001 NOT claimed; AWS; customer can choose region — Canada, US (multiple regions) or EU; data "cryptographically isolated" per carrier but no single-tenant option described; no pen-test statement; whether customer data trains shared models not addressed — [SortSpoke security](https://www.sortspoke.com/security)
- Third-party profile: models "train in under a day with as few as 10 documents"; integrates "with actuarial systems for loss run data"; founded 2017, Toronto, CEO Jasper Li, 10 employees as of Dec 2024 — [idp-software.com SortSpoke profile](https://idp-software.com/vendors/sortspoke/) (profile dated Aug 2025, modified 2026)
- Celent directory: automates extraction from applications, SOVs and loss runs with HITL workflows; HQ 111 Peter Street, Toronto; ownership includes Idea Partners, SixThirty and Great American Insurance Group Ventures — [Celent SortSpoke listing](https://www.celent.com/en/directory/companies/sort-spoke)

**Convr (formerly DataCubes)**
- Homepage: modular AI underwriting workbench on the "Risk Context Engine (RCE)" (commercial P&C ontology/knowledge graph); modules Intake, Workflow, Risk 360, d3 Desk, Answers, Scores, Insights, Convr AI; models "trained on" ACORD forms, SOVs, loss runs, broker emails, supplemental apps; reviewer workflows with confidence scoring, side-by-side document comparison, exception queues; logs reviewer actions and data lineage; "modern APIs with standardized JSON outputs," PAS/rating-engine integration, and MCP support; implementation 4-6 weeks for submission-to-triage, ~90 days for portfolio-connected underwriting; security certifications and hosting NOT mentioned; WC not mentioned — [Convr homepage](https://www.convr.com/)
- Platform page: "the same document should produce the same structured output each time"; 91% machine-read accuracy (Tangram case study); supports explainability expectations in the NAIC Model Bulletin; notes a loss run's "reserve" column is not a paid amount; hosting, deployment model, certifications, encryption and retention NOT mentioned — [Convr platform page](https://www.convr.com/platform/)
- Intake AI page: loss runs explicitly supported; IDP with ML splits, classifies, extracts and normalizes into a standardized submission schema "regardless of document format"; no published accuracy rate; confidence scoring "assesses input quality and guides review"; reviewers correct in-line, corrections feed model improvement; processing "seconds to minutes"; data available via UI, Excel views and "open APIs"; MCP integration; how unfamiliar layouts are onboarded is not explained; WC not mentioned — [Convr Intake](https://www.convr.com/intake/)
- Repeatability post (Oct 13, 2026): ingestion models "built and tested for repeatability ... the same document produces the same structured output every time," attributed to models "trained specifically on these document types" plus the ontology; no methodology or metrics given; architecture (LLM vs trained) not stated — [Convr, purpose-built workbench vs general LLM](https://www.convr.com/blog/why-a-purpose-built-underwriting-workbench-beats-a-general-purpose-llm/)
- Audit trail post (Sep 28, 2026): "record of every reviewer action," "source-linked data lineage"; exportable logs not mentioned — [Convr audit trail post](https://www.convr.com/blog/build-an-audit-trail-around-every-ai-assisted-decision/)
- Third-party profile: inputs PDF, Excel, Word, email; JSON output through the ontology engine; API connections to policy systems, rating engines, Excel and BindHQ; claims "97% extraction accuracy" aggregate across document types and "processing in about 30 seconds"; no loss-run-specific accuracy; deployment options not specified — [idp-software.com Convr profile](https://idp-software.com/vendors/convr/) (profile Aug 2025, modified Apr 2026)
- Generative AI module (Mar 17, 2026): conversational assistant embedded in the workbench, built on the "Convr Context Engine"; can update the submission, create tasks; no loss-run specifics — [Convr press release via WOWK/Cision](https://digital-release.wowktv.com/business/press-releases/cision/20260317CG09801/convr-ai-powers-underwriters-with-actionable-insights-faster)
- Agentic update (Beinsure, Aug 12, 2026): four workflow agents (referral, declination, financial analyst, underwriting authority) with adjustable authority; ontology outputs structured JSON, developed since 2016; Beinsure analysts caveat adoption is "Maybe slower than vendors claim" — [Beinsure, Convr agentic underwriting](https://beinsure.com/news/insurtech-convr-ai-agentic-underwriting/)
- Convr security page and trust.convr.com could not be fetched (client error / robots disallowed), and no SOC 2 / ISO 27001 statement for Convr was found in any fetched source — [convr.com/security (fetch failed)](https://www.convr.com/security); [trust.convr.com (robots disallowed)](https://trust.convr.com/)

**Cross-vendor context on the hard parts**
- Insurance Thought Leadership (Jul 29, 2026): loss runs vary by provider, claim descriptions use abbreviations, severity signals can be buried in narrative; recommends three authorization levels (automated low-risk with deterministic checks, human approval for recommendations, human decisions on eligibility/pricing); first half of intake can realistically reach 90-95% STP; recommends decoupling AI from core systems through an integration layer — [ITL, Making AI Work in Commercial Submission Intake](https://www.insurancethoughtleadership.com/ai-machine-learning/making-ai-work-commercial-submission-intake)
- Quantiphi (Aug 28, 2026): failure modes are carrier template variance, low-resolution scans/handwriting, missing fields, inconsistent terminology, duplicate claims; multi-tab Excel and password-protected files not discussed; a build consists of OCR + NLP/LLM + validation layer (confidence scoring, business rules, consistency checks, exception routing) + ingestion/workflow/analytics/integration layers — [Quantiphi loss run automation](https://quantiphi.com/blog/loss-run-automation/)
- V7 (Jul 5, 2026, vendor-authored): "every carrier uses its own layout," same field carries different labels (amount paid vs indemnity paid); template-based approaches struggle; comparison table lists V7 Go, SortSpoke (HITL + PAS integration), Pibit.ai (frequency/severity analytics), Roots.ai (pre-built carrier-format models, BPO replacement), CogniSure (trend dashboards), BPO services; Nomad, Convr and Sensible not mentioned — [V7 loss run analysis article](https://www.v7labs.com/blog/ai-loss-run-analysis-automate-data-extraction)

### Inferences
- The insurer's Use Case 1 (self-serve upload → no-human real-time quote) is explicitly **against** SortSpoke's design philosophy ("human oversight on every field," "shallow" integration beside the PAS) and is not something Nomad documents; Bevaya and Convr are the only two of the four with documented confidence-threshold-driven straight-through paths (Bevaya ">90% no-touch" in production; Convr "extracted data flows into underwriting workflows without manual copying").
- Use Case 2's embedded analytics (what-if sliders, feature lineage to the pricing engine, CA cumulative-trauma mix) is not offered by any of the four; vendors stop at field-level source lineage and basic loss summaries (large loss, open/closed, totals). The build side can differentiate here, and a vendor would need the insurer to build the analytics layer on top of vendor JSON anyway.
- Bevaya's benchmark cost basis (B200 GPU minutes, 8 workers, ~21 s/loss run) implies its loss-run model is a self-hosted fine-tuned model rather than a frontier-API wrapper; this is the strongest technical moat among the four and is the number the build side must beat or explain (93.1% raw macro field accuracy on 346 mixed-LOB loss runs).
- Convr's "same document → same structured output" claim and Bevaya's "pinned model version + rerun" are the two closest things to deterministic re-extraction; neither claims carrier template memory per se. SortSpoke's "pretrained loss run models, no template setup" and Sensible's SenseML configs (see Q4) are the two ends of the template spectrum.
- Only Bevaya is Azure-hosted, which may matter to the insurer's Azure architect for network peering/Private Link, but Bevaya explicitly does not offer on-prem or customer-tenant deployment, so "deploy into our Azure tenant" is a no for all four based on public information.

### Gaps
- No public API reference (endpoints, auth, webhook payloads, JSON schema) was retrievable for any of the four; docs.bevaya.ai returned empty, SortSpoke and Nomad have none, Convr says "open APIs" only.
- Convr's SOC 2/ISO status, hosting provider and data residency are unpublished and both security pages were unreachable.
- Nomad's hosting provider, LLM subprocessors and data residency are unpublished (trust center is a JS shell).
- Bevaya's per-LOB (incl. WC) and per-field benchmark numbers exist only in an interactive dashboard and a labs.bevaya.ai write-up that is robots-blocked; the WC-specific accuracy could not be retrieved.
- No vendor describes handling of password-protected PDFs except SortSpoke; none describes multi-tab XLSX handling explicitly.

## Key Question 2: What is known about pricing models and typical contract size? Any public pricing, case studies, or customer quotes?

### Takeaway
Two of the four publish list pricing: Bevaya (per-agent subscription at $4,000/agent/month billed annually plus a pooled credit model where 1 credit = 1 standard page) and Nomad Data ("starting at $3K/month," volume/complexity-scaled). SortSpoke and Convr are quote-only; the only external pricing anchor for a comparable pure-extraction API is Sensible ($449-$1,349/month, ~$0.53-$0.57/doc overage).

### Cited Findings
- **Bevaya**: "Per AI agent pricing. Shared credits. Scales as you grow." Deploying an agent costs $4,000/month per the bundle calculator (headline says "starting at $0 per AI agent per month, billed annually"); discounts 5% (2 agents), 10% (3 agents; example $10,800/mo), up to 20% (4+); every agent includes pooled credits (page inconsistently says 200,000 or 100,000), full platform access, AI Assistant/Canvas, enterprise integrations (Guidewire, Duck Creek, OnBase), SOC 2 Type 2; 1 credit = extracting one standard document page; classification 1 credit/page; cross-document extraction 4 credits; endorsement 20 credits; FNOL setup 60 credits; additional credit tiers: Starter up to 1M credits (no discount; "pilots and specialty carriers"), Growth up to 5M (5% off), Scale up to 25M (10%), Enterprise up to 100M (15%), >100M custom; annual billing only; no minimums stated; no free trial/POC terms — [Bevaya pricing](https://www.bevaya.ai/pricing)
- **Nomad Data**: Doc Chat "Starting at $3K/month," "scales with volume of documents and complexity of processing"; no rate card, tiers, per-page or per-seat pricing; no pilot/POC terms; Nomad-hosted managed service; ROI calculator defaults 25,000 cases/yr, 100 pages/case, 8 hours/case — [Nomad pricing](https://www.nomad-data.com/pricing)
- **SortSpoke**: no pricing published; "cost scales with documents, not people" — [SortSpoke loss runs page](https://www.sortspoke.com/solutions/loss-runs); pricing page fetch failed — [SortSpoke pricing (fetch failed)](https://www.sortspoke.com/pricing); G2 shows zero reviews and "pricing not currently available" — [G2 SortSpoke](https://www.g2.com/it/products/sortspoke/reviews)
- **Convr**: pricing "Custom," request a quote; only an ROI calculator and demo request on the site — [Zoftware Convr plans](https://zoftwarehub.com/products/convr/plans); [Convr homepage](https://www.convr.com/)
- **Comparable extraction-API pricing (Sensible)**: Growth $449/mo (750 docs, $0.57/doc overage), Scale $1,349/mo (3,200 docs, $0.53/doc), Enterprise custom at 10,000+ docs/mo with custom SLA, BAA, retention and region; 14-day free trial; per-page pricing possible for high-volume single-page docs — [Sensible pricing](https://www.sensible.so/pricing)
- **Comparable managed-service listing (IntellectAI)**: "Intellect Magic Loss Runs AI Agent Managed Service" on AWS Marketplace, custom private-offer pricing only, delivered as a Docker container for ECS/EKS via professional services — [AWS Marketplace, Intellect Magic Loss Runs](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-y322njplrmgos)
- **Comparable SI offering (Deloitte)**: "Agentic AI-driven Submission Intake" with a dedicated Loss Run Agent on Bedrock, custom pricing, professional services — [AWS Marketplace, Deloitte agentic intake](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-mtfsi3ii2jfos)
- **Customer quotes (SortSpoke)**: RGA VP Underwriting Business Solutions: "SortSpoke has made one of the messiest and most manual problems in underwriting easy to solve"; Assistant VP of Analytics (unnamed): "SortSpoke is my favorite vendor by far"; P&C Manager: "The system is intuitive, so there was limited training" — [SortSpoke case studies](https://www.sortspoke.com/case-studies)
- **Customer quotes (Bevaya)**: Eastern Alliance SVP IS Harry Talbert: "Bevaya's AI agents reduced our claims indexing from 5 days to under an hour" (claims, not loss runs) — [Bevaya Eastern Alliance case study](https://www.bevaya.ai/case-studies/eastern-alliance-claims-document-indexing-ai-agent)
- **Customer quotes (Nomad)**: GAIG's Rachelle Leone: "Nomad finds it instantly, and that is such a huge time saver" (claims file review, 70% faster review cycles; not loss runs) — [Nomad GAIG case study PDF](https://landing.nomad-data.com/hubfs/Case%20Study-GAIG.pdf?hsLang=en)
- **Customer quotes (Convr)**: Convr CEO John Stammen on PERMA: "our implementation was completed in just one month" — [PERMA / Convr press release](https://www.streetinsider.com/PRNewswire/PERMA+Places+Trust+in+Convr+AI%C2%AE+Underwriting+Solution+Intake+AI/25146656.html)

### Inferences
- Rough Bevaya sizing for the insurer: one Loss Run Processing agent ≈ $48K/yr list before credits; at 1 credit/page and the insurer's ~50,000-document two-year archive (from the user's memory file), a 20-page average would be ~1M pages ≈ the "Starter" tier; a second agent (e.g., Submission Intake) adds another ~$45.6K/yr at the 5% discount. This is an inference from list prices, not a quote.
- Nomad's $3K/month floor makes it the cheapest entry point but, as a managed service with no published API, the insurer would likely be buying a white-glove configured workflow rather than a self-serve embeddable extractor.
- The absence of any public SortSpoke or Convr pricing plus Convr's "ROI within one policy term year" language suggests platform-subscription deals sized to underwriting headcount rather than per-document.

### Gaps
- No typical contract size, ACV or minimum commitment is public for SortSpoke or Convr; no third-party pricing reviews exist (G2 has zero SortSpoke reviews).
- No vendor publishes per-document or per-page unit pricing for loss runs specifically except via Bevaya's credit table.
- The web-search budget was exhausted before pricing could be sought for Kalepa, Indico or Insurance Quantified.

## Key Question 3: Which carriers/insurers are public reference customers? Any workers' comp specifically, and any California WC?

### Takeaway
Convr has the deepest public WC footprint (LUBA Workers' Comp, PERMA, KEMI, WCF Mutual, AF Group, Encova); Bevaya names Eastern Alliance (WC specialist) and Zenith (a California-headquartered WC carrier) as logos plus an unnamed "nationwide workers' compensation" intake customer; SortSpoke's references are Great American Custom, RGA, Sompo, SCM, OneDigital and a Canadian P&C carrier with no WC-specific reference; Nomad's named insurance references (GAIG, Continental General) are claims-side, not loss runs. No vendor publishes a California WC loss-run reference customer.

### Cited Findings
- **Convr**: LUBA Workers' Comp (regional WC carrier, Baton Rouge LA) live on the AI Underwriting Workbench with Risk Context Engine, extracting data from ACORD forms, loss runs and broker emails; integrated with Sapiens; press release Aug 19, 2026 — [TechIntelPro, LUBA goes live with Convr](https://techintelpro.com/news/luba-workers-comp-goes-live-with-convr-to-advance-underwriting-with-ai); [BriefGlance LUBA summary](https://briefglance.com/companies/convr-inc/pulses/70392)

## Key Question 4: How do they handle human-in-the-loop review, confidence scoring, and "learning" a carrier format? Do any claim carrier template memory or deterministic re-extraction?

### Takeaway
All four route low-confidence fields to human review, but only Bevaya documents the full loop (per-field calibrated confidence, immutable override log with confidence-at-decision-time, X-Ray coordinates, corrections feeding retraining, pinned model versions with reproducible re-runs). Convr is the only one to claim repeatability ("same document → same structured output every time"); none of the four claims explicit per-carrier template memory — SortSpoke and Nomad position as template-free, while Sensible (a non-shortlisted competitor) is the clearest template/config-based approach with "configs built in hours."

### Cited Findings
- **Bevaya HITL**: thresholds per field and per flow set without code; routing combines confidence with business rules (missing documents, appetite, duplicates); recommendation to "start from your accuracy SLA, then tune as models learn"; review queue with auto/manual assignment, aging metrics; each reviewer action records original AI output, reviewer ID, corrected value, timestamp, confidence at decision time, review duration; logs immutable and exportable; override rates tracked per field; corrections "captured, audited, validated, and used to improve later extractions"; "selective recompute"; retraining "without taking the flow offline"; "the review queue shrinks the longer the platform runs" (no figures) — [Bevaya Human-in-the-Loop](https://www.bevaya.ai/platform/human-in-the-loop)
- **Bevaya format learning**: "Insurance domain experts curate the InsurGPT models and add coverage for new forms, schedules, and document variants"; drift detection flags changes; "new field mappings roll out on a regular cadence"; models retrained on new data including freshly handled documents; thresholds and routing tuned on the customer's own files — [Bevaya implementation](https://www.bevaya.ai/implementation)
- **Bevaya reproducibility**: "Model, flow, and training-data versions are pinned to each run"; "any historical item can be rerun against its original model and flow to validate a past outcome"; no determinism claim — [Bevaya Responsible AI](https://www.bevaya.ai/responsible-ai)
- **Bevaya benchmark note**: production pipeline adds a "second verification model" on top of the loss run model; ">90% completed with no human touch" in production — [Bevaya benchmark press release](https://www.bevaya.ai/news/bevaya-benchmark-insurance-trained-ai-beats-frontier-models-on-loss-runs-insurances-hardest-documents)
- **SortSpoke HITL**: customer sets confidence thresholds; fields above accepted, rest to the customer's own reviewers ("no vendor review pool"); each value traces to source location; audit trail of who reviewed/what changed/when; "no per-carrier templates ... pretrained loss run models and template-free extraction read each layout as it arrives" — [SortSpoke loss runs page](https://www.sortspoke.com/solutions/loss-runs); ML learns "based on underwriter feedback" — [SortSpoke data extraction](https://www.sortspoke.com/platform/data-extraction); third-party profile says models "train in under a day with as few as 10 documents" — [idp-software.com SortSpoke profile](https://idp-software.com/vendors/sortspoke/)
- **Convr HITL**: confidence scoring "assesses input quality and guides review"; reviewers validate/correct in-line; "corrections feed model improvement while preserving auditability"; side-by-side document comparison and exception queues — [Convr Intake](https://www.convr.com/intake/); repeatability: "built and tested for repeatability ... same document produces the same structured output every time" (no methodology) — [Convr repeatability post](https://www.convr.com/blog/why-a-purpose-built-underwriting-workbench-beats-a-general-purpose-llm/)
- **Nomad HITL**: no formal review workflow published; "uncertain extractions are surfaced for human review"; "staff corrections ... improve the system over time"; no confidence scores mentioned; "Nomad Process"/white-glove: interviews, extraction rules tested on historical docs, post-launch monitoring — [Nomad portfolio loss-run page](https://www.nomad-data.com/doc-chat/ai-driven-loss-run-analysis-unlocking-portfolio-level-risk-insights-in-minutes); claims "no pre-defined templates or training on your document types" while onboarding includes "document schema mapping" — [Nomad underwriting loss-run page](https://www.nomad-data.com/doc-chat/unlocking-faster-risk-assessment-ai-for-loss-run-analysis-in-commercial-insurance-underwriting)
- **Sensible (template/config approach, for contrast)**: "LLM parsing for degraded inputs with deterministic rules"; pre-built loss run templates in a config library written in SenseML "make each layout repeatable"; new carrier formats "built in hours," managed services write and maintain configs; schema-enforced JSON with per-field `source` (page + bounding box); REST API, Python/Node SDKs, webhook/polling; "most production deployments achieve 95%+ accuracy"; low-confidence flagged, thresholds configurable — [Sensible loss runs page](https://sensible.so/extract/loss-runs); Shepherd: 9 carrier formats, "100% extraction accuracy across supported formats," 351-page Travelers loss run in 31 s, engineers learned SenseML and used the "section method" with user-defined bounding boxes; "exploring LLM approaches for unknown or novel formats" — [Sensible Shepherd case study](https://www.sensible.so/customers/shepherd)
- **CogniSure (dated, 2020)**: claimed to have "learned the loss run formats of the top 25 P&C insurers" with a target of the top 100 by year-end 2020 — the clearest historical claim of per-carrier format memory — [Claims Journal, CogniSure launches loss run analytics (Oct 1, 2020)](https://www.claimsjournal.com/?p=299672) (dated)
- **IntellectAI (dated 2024)**: "tested on over 1,000 carrier formats, with ongoing testing and adjustments every day"; trained humans review output "to prevent LLM hallucinations" — [IntellectAI Loss Runs Overview PDF (May 2024)](https://www.intellectai.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Loss-Runs-Overview.pdf) (dated)
- **Kalepa**: "no up-front model training"; validation via document-linked evidence, cross-document consistency checks, confidence-driven controls; Amrisc reported accuracy "in the mid-to-high 90s in a proof of concept" — [Kalepa submission ingestion](https://kalepa.com/platforms/submission-ingestion)
- **Indico (dated 2020)**: transfer learning, "model can be trained on a few dozen sample reports," ~95% of documents processed without help — [Indico loss run blog (Sep 24, 2020)](https://indicodata.ai/blog/reduce-loss-run-reporting-costs-with-intelligent-automation/) (dated)

### Inferences
- "Learning a format so repeat documents are cheaper" is a pricing concept none of the four exposes: Bevaya charges the same credits per page regardless of whether the carrier has been seen; the only vendor where repeat formats are structurally cheaper is Sensible (deterministic config reuse), which is exactly the architecture a build side on Azure (Document Intelligence custom models + per-carrier config + LLM fallback) could replicate.
- Bevaya's "confidence at decision time" + per-field override rates is the most complete answer to the insurer's "audit log of overrides" requirement; the build side should match the exact record fields listed (original value, reviewer ID, corrected value, timestamp, confidence, duration).
- Convr's repeatability claim is unsubstantiated but is the kind of claim an evaluator can test cheaply (re-submit the same PDF N times and diff JSON); the build side can make the same claim credibly if it uses deterministic templates + temperature-0 LLM fallback with hashing.

### Gaps
- No vendor publishes how confidence scores are calculated or calibrated, nor measured false-accept rates at a given threshold.
- No vendor quantifies how much the review queue shrinks over time.
- Whether SortSpoke's "10 documents, under a day" training is per-carrier or per-document-type is unclear.

## Key Question 5: What do customers and analysts say are their weaknesses?

### Takeaway
There is almost no independent customer-review signal (G2 has zero SortSpoke reviews; no G2/Capterra reviews surfaced for Bevaya, Nomad or Convr), so weaknesses must be inferred from structural facts: Nomad's tiny team and seed-stage funding, SortSpoke's ~10-person headcount and human-review-first design, Convr's unpublished security posture and workbench-centric packaging, and Bevaya's SaaS-only/no-tenant deployment plus vendor-run-only benchmarks.

### Cited Findings
- **SortSpoke**: G2 page says "SortSpoke hasn't been reviewed yet," zero reviews, listed under OCR with seller "Mocsy" — [G2 SortSpoke](https://www.g2.com/it/products/sortspoke/reviews); headcount 10 (Dec 2024), total raised $4.55M, profile flags "small headcount may matter for enterprise support" and that accuracy/speed figures are unverified — [idp-software.com SortSpoke profile](https://idp-software.com/vendors/sortspoke/); [CB Insights SortSpoke](https://www.cbinsights.com/company/sortspoke); the Optalitix partnership (Apr 7, 2025) exists because "SortSpoke users had to manually load extracted submission data into their underwriting models" before it — [Optalitix / SortSpoke partnership](https://www.optalitix.com/insights/optalitix-partners-with-sortspoke-to-revolutionise-underwriting-with-ai-powered-document-processing); day-one integration is "Shallow, deliberately" — [SortSpoke submission triage](https://www.sortspoke.com/platform/submission-triage)
- **Nomad Data**: ~15 employees, $3.2M seed (Dec 2022) is the only disclosed funding; company pivoted from a data-marketplace (Connect) to an AI platform with Doc Chat in 2024 — [yespress Nomad profile](https://yespress.io/nomad-data); [Struck Capital seed announcement](https://struckcapital.com/nomad-data-announces-3-2m-seed-funding/); homepage testimonials attributed to the same name with different titles/companies, "so their attribution is unclear" — [Nomad homepage](https://www.nomad-data.com/); no accuracy metrics on any loss-run page and multiple unsupported claims ("250,000 pages per minute," "up to 85%," "Rapid ROI ... less than one quarter") — [Nomad underwriting loss-run page](https://www.nomad-data.com/doc-chat/unlocking-faster-risk-assessment-ai-for-loss-run-analysis-in-commercial-insurance-underwriting); dozens of near-duplicate SEO loss-run pages exist (e.g., multiple "streamlining loss run report analysis ... workers compensation" URLs) — [Nomad loss-run SEO page A](https://www.nomad-data.com/doc-chat/streamlining-loss-run-report-analysis-for-aggregate-risk-trends-in-workers-compensation-general-liability-construction-and-commercial-auto-a-guide-for-the-underwriting-manager); [Nomad loss-run SEO page B](https://www.nomad-data.com/doc-chat/streamlining-loss-run-report-analysis-for-aggregate-risk-trends-in-workers-compensation-general-liability-construction-and-commercial-auto-a-guide-for-the-underwriting-manager-3c9d3)
- **Convr**: founded 2016 (as DataCubes, Schaumburg IL), $17.7M raised through a Nov 2019 Series B led by Stage 2 Capital; no later rounds listed — [Seedtable DataCubes funding](https://seedtable.com/companies/datacubes/funding-rounds/series-b-2019-11); profile lists "$15-18.2M" raised, pricing/headcount/deployment undisclosed, 97% accuracy "lacks a stated methodology" — [idp-software.com Convr profile](https://idp-software.com/vendors/convr/); homepage and platform pages contain no SOC 2/ISO/hosting statement — [Convr platform page](https://www.convr.com/platform/); data-lake size inconsistently stated (85M vs 87M) — [Convr platform page](https://www.convr.com/platform/); Convr's own build-vs-buy post cites unnamed "analysts have verified there is nothing else on the market that compares" — [Convr build vs buy post](https://www.convr.com/blog/build-vs-buy-is-in-house-ai-underwriting-as-easy-as-it-seems/)
- **Bevaya**: SaaS only, no on-prem, no customer-tenant option, "logical boundary" isolation — [Bevaya security](https://www.bevaya.ai/security); benchmark is self-run with no independent verification and a Pareto chart that "excludes Bevaya's model" — [Bevaya benchmarks](https://www.bevaya.ai/benchmarks); pricing page gives conflicting included-credit figures (200,000 vs 100,000) and a "$0/agent" headline vs $4,000/agent calculator — [Bevaya pricing](https://www.bevaya.ai/pricing); Eastern Alliance case study contradicts itself on hours saved (22,000+ vs 2,700+) — [Bevaya Eastern Alliance case study](https://www.bevaya.ai/case-studies/eastern-alliance-claims-document-indexing-ai-agent); HFS (Sep 20, 2024) framed risks as legacy-integration complexity and the need for governance on accuracy/transparency; 35 customers at the time — [HFS Research Roots Series B highlight](https://www.hfsresearch.com/research/hfs-hot-tech-star-roots-automation-seriesb-funding/) (dated)
- **Industry-wide**: pilots stall because they prove accuracy but not production workflow fit ("pilot thinking"); off-the-shelf tools "often add another isolated interface"; loss-run narrative content may be missed even when read correctly — [ITL, Making AI Work in Commercial Submission Intake](https://www.insurancethoughtleadership.com/ai-machine-learning/making-ai-work-commercial-submission-intake); Beinsure: agentic underwriting adoption "Maybe slower than vendors claim" — [Beinsure, Convr agentic underwriting](https://beinsure.com/news/insurtech-convr-ai-agentic-underwriting/)
- **Celent**: both Celent "Gen AI in P&C Underwriting" showcase pages (Groundspeed/IQ May 15, 2024; IntellectAI Aug 20, 2024) contain vendor demos only, "no independent Celent assessment" — [Celent IQ/Groundspeed showcase](https://www.celent.com/en/insights/272527614); [Celent IntellectAI showcase](https://www.celent.com/en/insights/654869187) (both dated)

### Inferences
- Viability risk ranking (lowest to highest) based on disclosed capital and scale: Bevaya ($22.2M Series B 2024, 100+ staff, Inc. 5000 2025 and 2026) < Convr (last disclosed round 2019 but steady 2025-26 customer announcements) < SortSpoke ($4.55M total, ~10 staff) ≈ Nomad ($3.2M seed, ~15 staff). A March 2026 RFP "failure" (per the user) is consistent with small vendors struggling to meet enterprise security/integration asks.
- Lack of CA WC specifics is universal: no vendor mentions cumulative trauma, WCIRB, or CA-specific claim typing; this is a clear build-side differentiator the insurer's underwriters will value.
- Schema customisation: SortSpoke and Sensible expose customer-defined fields; Bevaya's loss-run agent emits a fixed "20-column" merged policy table and claims table; Convr normalizes into "a standardized submission schema." A fixed schema is a lock-in and feature-engineering constraint for Use Case 2.

### Gaps
- No independent customer reviews or analyst (Celent/Datos/Gartner) ratings for any of the four were found; Celent VendorMatch content is paywalled.
- Convr's current funding/ownership since 2019 is unknown; whether it is profitable or PE-backed could not be determined.
- No public evidence of layoffs at any of the four.

## Key Question 6: What do demos/POCs typically look like, and what do vendors ask the prospect to provide?

### Takeaway
Public materials describe three patterns: Nomad's no-integration drag-and-drop pilot in 1-2 weeks; Bevaya's three-phase Discover/Build-and-Validate/Live engagement (4-12 weeks, tuned on the customer's real files, ops sign-off before go-live); and SortSpoke's self-serve 30-minute sign-up-to-extraction with customer reviewers. Convr promises 4-6 weeks to a first triage workflow and a one-month PERMA implementation. No vendor publishes a formal POC acceptance protocol or asks explicitly for ground-truth labels.

### Cited Findings
- **Nomad**: offers a 30-minute demo or "Talk to Sales"; loss-run page offers "a no-integration drag-and-drop pilot first," with results in one to two weeks — [Nomad pricing](https://www.nomad-data.com/pricing); [Nomad loss-run page (WC/auto/GL)](https://www.nomad-data.com/doc-chat/automating-loss-run-report-analysis-for-workers-compensation-commercial-auto-and-general-liability-construction-reducing-leakage-and-improving-reserve-accuracy-for-loss-control-analysts); white-glove onboarding interviews underwriters/analysts, tests extraction rules against historical documents — [Nomad portfolio loss-run page](https://www.nomad-data.com/doc-chat/ai-driven-loss-run-analysis-unlocking-portfolio-level-risk-insights-in-minutes); Doc Chat go-live "as little as 5 days" — [Nomad Doc Chat page](https://www.nomad-data.com/doc-chat)
- **Bevaya**: phases Discover & Design (workflow mapping, systems inventory), Build & Validate (configure pre-built or custom agent, integrate, "tune it on real files," ops leaders sign off), Live & Improve; "Most deployments go live in 4 to 12 weeks," first production results "in as little as 3 weeks" for pre-built agents; customer provides frontline SMEs, real submissions/claims files for tuning, IT for system access and security sign-off; integrations via APIs, SFTP or Outlook; no labeling/ground-truth process described; consulting partner may lead — [Bevaya implementation](https://www.bevaya.ai/implementation); "Starter" credit tier is explicitly for "pilots and specialty carriers" — [Bevaya pricing](https://www.bevaya.ai/pricing); AI assistant builds agents from natural-language prompts; "product tour" available — [Coverager, Roots launches Bevaya](https://coverager.com/roots-launches-new-ai-agent-platform/)
- **SortSpoke**: "about 30 minutes to go from sign-up to extracting loss runs"; customer's own reviewers verify; demo request is the CTA — [SortSpoke loss runs page](https://www.sortspoke.com/solutions/loss-runs); "models train in under a day with as few as 10 documents" — [idp-software.com SortSpoke profile](https://idp-software.com/vendors/sortspoke/); intake by forwarded email or upload, output CSV or API — [SortSpoke submission triage](https://www.sortspoke.com/platform/submission-triage)
- **Convr**: "initial submission-to-triage workflow in 4-6 weeks, portfolio-connected underwriting within about 90 days," ROI calculator and demo request — [Convr homepage](https://www.convr.com/); "speed-to-market blueprint" planned before work begins — [Convr build vs buy post](https://www.convr.com/blog/build-vs-buy-is-in-house-ai-underwriting-as-easy-as-it-seems/); PERMA implementation "completed in just one month" — [PERMA / Convr press release](https://www.streetinsider.com/PRNewswire/PERMA+Places+Trust+in+Convr+AI%C2%AE+Underwriting+Solution+Intake+AI/25146656.html)
- **Comparator POC signal (Kalepa)**: Amrisc's engineering lead reported accuracy "in the mid-to-high 90s in a proof of concept" — [Kalepa submission ingestion](https://kalepa.com/platforms/submission-ingestion)
- **Comparator POC signal (Sensible)**: 14-day free trial with full extraction/validation/config editor, no credit card — [Sensible pricing](https://www.sensible.so/pricing)
- **Guidance on POC design**: compare AI-assisted vs manual cases before launch; track quote-to-bind, referral, missing-data, correction and override rates after rollout — [ITL, Making AI Work in Commercial Submission Intake](https://www.insurancethoughtleadership.com/ai-machine-learning/making-ai-work-commercial-submission-intake)

### Inferences
- Vendors will ask for a representative sample of real loss runs (Bevaya says "real files"; Nomad "historical documents"); none asks for labeled ground truth up front, which means the insurer's bake-off ground truth (the archive's prior user-entered data, per the user's plan) is an asset the build side controls and can use to score every vendor on identical terms.
- Bevaya's "operations leaders must sign off before go-live" and Convr's 4-6 week minimum make a like-for-like timed bake-off favour the build side if the internal POC v1/v2 already exists (per the user's memory, v1 and v2 are built).

### Gaps
- No vendor publishes a POC scorecard, acceptance thresholds, or sample-size requirements.
- Whether any vendor will run a free/paid POC on de-identified documents without a contract is not public.

## Key Question 7: Funding, acquisitions, layoffs, or product pivots in 2025-2026 affecting viability

### Takeaway
Bevaya rebranded from Roots Automation (May 2026) on the back of a $22.2M Series B (Sep 2024), reported 100% YoY revenue growth in 2024 and 100+ staff, and made the Inc. 5000 in both 2025 and 2026; Convr has no disclosed funding since 2019 but a steady drumbeat of 2025-26 customer wins and product launches; SortSpoke and Nomad remain seed-scale. In the wider field, Federato raised a $100M Series D (Nov 2025), Sixfold $30M Series B (Jan 2026), Indico took strategic money from Aviva Ventures (Oct 2025), Pibit.ai raised $7M (Nov 2025), Applied Systems acquired Cytora (Sep 2025), and Groundspeed was absorbed by Insurance Quantified (2023); Chisel AI shut down in 2022.

### Cited Findings

### Inferences
- The "Insurity/Groundspeed" framing in the prompt is outdated: Groundspeed belongs to Insurance Quantified (Two Sigma IQ); Insurity was a channel partner in the AF Group deployment.
- Nomad's pivot history (marketplace → Doc Chat) and seed-only funding make it the highest execution risk for a multi-year embedded dependency; the build side can argue total-cost-of-ownership includes vendor continuity.

### Gaps
- Convr's post-2019 capitalization is unknown.

## Other notable competitors: inclusion/exclusion and one-line profiles

### Takeaway
Confirmed loss-run ingestion vendors beyond the four: Insurance Quantified/Groundspeed, Kalepa, Indico Data, Sensible, Pibit.ai, IntellectAI (Magic Submission), Concirrus (Loss Run Intelligence), CogniSure. Federato and Sixfold are workbench/decisioning platforms that consume extracted data from partners; Cytora is now inside Applied Systems; Chisel AI is defunct.

### Cited Findings
- **Insurance Quantified / Groundspeed**: Groundspeed ingests prior-carrier loss runs, delivers loss summaries and claim-level detail, identifies frequency and severity; library of specialized models on a contributory loss-run dataset; HITL exceptions; "fast data in minutes" or comprehensive data "in a couple of hours"; 3 of top 5 commercial carriers — [Celent Groundspeed VendorMatch](https://celent.com/vendormatch/discovery/solutions/988909439); [Celent IQ/Groundspeed showcase](https://www.celent.com/en/insights/272527614); IQ homepage: "normalize loss run data," 1M+ documents/yr, WC in production, logos incl. Republic Indemnity — [Insurance Quantified homepage](https://www.insurancequantified.com/)
- **Kalepa**: ingestion by email auto-forward, portal or API; classifies and extracts from "hundreds of document types" incl. complex loss runs; "no up-front model training"; "AI Ensemble Engine chooses the right model or method in real time"; outcomes 58% faster quote time, 30%+ premium per underwriter; logos Berkley, Paragon, Munich Re Specialty, Canopius, Bowhead, Church Mutual, Columbia, IAT, AmRisc, James River, Secura, Merchants; no security certs named; product-security page is only a disclosure policy — [Kalepa submission ingestion](https://kalepa.com/platforms/submission-ingestion); [Kalepa homepage](https://kalepa.com/); [Kalepa product security](https://kalepa.com/product-security)
- **Indico Data**: "Extraction Agents capture data from loss runs, SOVs, emails, and attachments"; 10+ input formats; "full auditability and human oversight"; logos Allstate, Aspen, Convex, Everest, Markel; no accuracy or deployment details — [Indico underwriting page](https://indicodata.ai/underwriting)
- **Sensible**: developer-first extraction API; see Q4 for approach; customers Neptune Flood, Vouch, Founder Shield, SterlingRisk, CompScience, Ledgebrook, Obie, Insurance Quantified, Shepherd; SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA; retention indefinite by default — [Sensible loss runs page](https://sensible.so/extract/loss-runs)
- **Pibit.ai**: "universal document ingestion" across any carrier/format; claims 99.9% field-level accuracy with source tracing; HDVI 96% reduction in loss-run analysis time; Kinetic WC case; ISO 27001 and "AICPA SOC Certified" per footer; no API documented — [Pibit.ai homepage](https://www.pibit.ai/)
- **IntellectAI**: Magic Submission with loss-run extraction, ">95% accuracy," handwriting/Excel/images/PDF, "tested on over 1,000 carrier formats," humans review to prevent hallucinations, LLM partnerships with Microsoft and AWS; AWS Marketplace managed-service container for ECS/EKS — [IntellectAI Loss Runs Overview PDF](https://www.intellectai.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/Loss-Runs-Overview.pdf) (dated 2024); [AWS Marketplace, Intellect Magic Loss Runs](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-y322njplrmgos); Feb 28, 2024 launch release — [IntellectAI loss-run press release](https://www.intellectai.com/intellectai-introduces-groundbreaking-technology-to-process-loss-runs-in-an-instant-with-greater-than-95-accuracy-and-no-touch) (dated)
- **Concirrus**: Loss Run Intelligence — ingest PDFs/spreadsheets/images, validate totals, "99% extraction accuracy," complex files under five minutes, rating-ready CSV or real-time API, batch merge of multiple loss runs per insured; UnitedRisk testimonial — [Concirrus Loss Run Intelligence](https://concirrus.ai/loss-run-intelligence/)
- **CogniSure**: Guidewire Marketplace listing — loss insights from PDF and Excel carrier loss runs, submission triage, turnkey implementation — [CogniSure Guidewire Marketplace PDF](https://marketplace.guidewire.com/sfc/servlet.shepherd/version/download/0683n00000D7HKdAAN); partnered with Federato (Jun 2023) — [Federato / CogniSure partnership](https://www.federato.ai/articles/cognisure-and-federato-announce-strategic-partnership-to-drive-commercial-lines-underwriting-transformation) (dated)
- **Federato (excluded as extractor)**: RiskOps workbench; relies on Groundspeed (Aug 2022) and CogniSure (Jun 2023) partnerships for extraction; Celent listing does not mention extraction — [Federato / Groundspeed partnership](https://www.federato.ai/articles/groundspeed-and-federato-launch-strategic-partnership) (dated); [Celent Federato listing](https://www.celent.com/directory/companies/federato)
- **Sixfold (excluded)**: "AI Underwriter" decisioning across 40+ LOBs; loss-run extraction not mentioned — [FinTech Global, Sixfold $30M](https://fintech.global/2026/01/30/insurtech-firm-sixfold-secures-30m-to-advance-ai-underwriting/)
- **Cytora (de-emphasised)**: acquired by Applied Systems Sep 2025; converts structured/unstructured submissions to transaction-ready data; loss runs not named — [Insurance Journal, Applied acquires Cytora](https://insurancejournal.com/news/national/2025/09/09/838445.htm)
- **Chisel AI (excluded)**: shut down April 2022 — [Coverager, Chisel AI shuts down](https://coverager.com/ai-software-startup-chisel-ai-shuts-down/) (dated)
- **Bold Penguin (minor)**: SubmissionLink used by a customer for loss-run summaries (six weeks → six minutes for ~80 accounts), 98%+ intake accuracy, no loss-run accuracy figure — [Bold Penguin loss run article](https://www.boldpenguin.com/news/loss-run-insurance)

### Inferences
- For a WC insurer wanting an embeddable extraction API feeding its own pricing engine and QMS, the closest architectural fits among competitors are Sensible (developer API, schema-enforced JSON, bounding-box lineage, webhooks) and Concirrus (real-time API to rating engine); the four shortlisted vendors are all closer to workflow/agent platforms.
- Insurance Quantified's combination of WC-in-production, Republic Indemnity (CA WC) logo and Groundspeed's loss-summary/frequency-severity outputs makes it the most relevant omitted vendor for the RFP; the build side should expect the insurer to be approached by IQ.

### Gaps
- Search budget prevented deeper profiles (security, pricing, API) for Insurance Quantified, Kalepa and Indico.
- Pibit.ai's SOC 2 type and Concirrus's security/deployment are unverified.
